Eight chapters, complete, copyedited, © Julian Jenkins / Cre8tive. This is the STORY authority for Episode 1 / Book 1. The v5 bible and Continuity Locks remain the WORLD authority; where the two touch, the manuscript wins on events, dialogue and order, the locks win on geometry, scale and appearance.
_why_this_file_exists: MP.B1 was directed on 2026-08-13 without this manuscript, from the bible's structure alone. It invented the opening. Julian caught it: the object has to ARRIVE, with Tom Chen, and he has to tell its story. Recorded so no beat is ever directed again from structure when the prose exists.

corrections_to_earlier_canon.was: MP.B1 opened on a 'bustle' of four invented tasks with Richard already carrying the box into the workshop.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.is: Ch.1 opens on 'Attempt Forty Seven' — Albert's door-knocking System, punchline 'There's nothing on the bench.' The box arrives in Ch.2 with Tom Chen, at the counter, on the shop floor.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.severity: structural — deletes the inciting incident and the man whose face carries the ending

corrections_to_earlier_canon.was: The box plays 'three halting notes, the third one sour' — reads as broken.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.is: A FRENCH TUNE, sweet and unmistakably wrong. 'Not broken wrong. Not clunk and jangle wrong.' The notes bend in odd places, the way a picture hangs crooked — and in exactly the same places every time. The sameness is the clue and the whole plot.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.severity: fatal to the story — a broken box can be fixed; a deliberately crooked one is the mystery

corrections_to_earlier_canon.was: Richard's apron read as 'both hands either side of the box, head slightly bowed'.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.is: Over the head, tied at the back, then both hands smoothing the front, 'like a knight settling his armour'. THEN, and only then, he lifts the box — and goes very still.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.severity: the series ritual, wrong in its first appearance

corrections_to_earlier_canon.was: Richard's line invented as 'Now then… what happened to you?'
corrections_to_earlier_canon.is: 'Nothing is truly broken. It just needs some TLC.' — said to the box, more than to Tom.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.severity: invented dialogue in a scripted show

corrections_to_earlier_canon.was: TP-03 v2 approved as the beat-1 opening keyframe.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.is: It depicts Richard carrying the box into the workshop past four children — a moment that does not occur in the manuscript. The plate is sound; its ROLE was wrong.
corrections_to_earlier_canon.severity: asset misassignment, not an art fault

world_facts_the_manuscript_settles.arcade_name: Llenast Passage — entered by a narrow iron arch on Castle Street between the bank and the pasty shop. NOT 'Castle Arcade'.
world_facts_the_manuscript_settles.shop_position: Three shops in from the Castle Street entrance, on the left of the ground-floor passage. Confirms the v5 lock; contradicts the legacy skill's upper gallery.
world_facts_the_manuscript_settles.sign: THISTLEWOOD'S: RESTORATIONS AND CURIOSITIES. ESTABLISHED 1922. / 'If it's broken, it belongs here.' Gold letters that have refused to fade for over a hundred years.
world_facts_the_manuscript_settles.macsen: Ginger cat. Sleeps in the BOOKSHOP window, not in Thistlewood's. Rose draws him from memory, adding one eye half open.
world_facts_the_manuscript_settles.the_good_chair: By the window, in the workshop. Rose's chair.
world_facts_the_manuscript_settles.brass_panel: In the doorframe. Richard adjusts it with a very small screwdriver, claiming each time that the clothes are nearly sorted. They never are.
world_facts_the_manuscript_settles.mrs_patel: Copper Kettle, brings tea across the arcade at three by the castle clock.
arc_seeds_ch8: The gold paint tin never gets emptier. Albert checked twice and drew lines.
Everything the door gives them is wrong — except Peggi's clogs, which fit.
A small wooden box on Richard's high shelf, behind the solvent jars. He looks at it when he thinks nobody sees.
